newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine gas firm to take part in pipeline revamp.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine gas firm to take part in pipeline revamp.

text.p: Ukrainian energy importing company United Energy Systems of Ukraine (UESU) plans to participate in a project to extend gas pipelines on the former Soviet republic's territory, its chief executive said on Tuesday.

Yulia Tymoshenko told a news conference that the company would expand the existing gas transit system serving Ukraine, and would invest in expanding the gas transit system which carries Russian gas to Europe.
The company accounts for around 30 percent of Ukraine's gas market and had reported turnover of $10 billion in 1996.

UESU has been the subject of media speculation regarding the possible role played in the company by Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko. But Tymoshenko denied suggestions that UESU may be enjoying Lazarenko's special protection.
"Pavlo Ivanovych (Lazarenko) is not a founder of our company," she said. "There are no facts to support this libel, nothing."
Tymoshenko denied last week in Washington a report in the New York Times which quoted Western intelligence sources as saying that Lazarenko has an interest in UESU.
"He has no shares. It's impossible," Tymoshenko said.
According to UESU information, the firm was aiming to import 15.5 billion cubic metres of Russian gas this year.
Last year the company imported 24.2 billion cubic metres (bcm) of Russian gas, and Tymoshenko said it paid the $2.1 billion bill in full, half of it through barter deals.
Tymoshenko said UESU would pay Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom with cash this year.
UESU also wants to sell gas for export, she added.
The State Oil and Gas Committee has said Ukraine would require 81 bcm of gas this year.
A company statement also said in 1996 UESU "secured" production of more than 1.5 million tonnes of metal products, accounting for about 10 percent of Ukraine's total production.
It also produced 500,000 tonnes of metal and steel tubing in 1996, the statement said, accounting for 25 percent of Ukraine's market.
